fields.sample_size: literature review and the authors' field observations and testimonies in Colombian territories; no systematic sample
fields.effect_estimate: Since 2016 Colombia's 'differential schemes' (norms, policies, statistical instruments and programmes) for water and sanitation in hard-to-reach urban zones and rural areas rest on an urban-rural dichotomy that does not match territorial complexity, socio-environmental conflict or the blurring urban-rural boundary; state responses are insufficient or inadequate, and the authors call for new concepts and categories (e.g. settlements and agglomerations) to improve territorial planning and access to public goods and enable community initiatives. Conceptual and observational; no outcome data.
fields.study_design: qualitative conceptual and observational analysis (literature plus field testimonies; no systematic methods)
fields.section: Full text: Introduction; literature on the urban-rural dichotomy; characterisation of territorial transformations; Conclusiones
fields.exact_location: Introduction; literature on the urban-rural dichotomy; characterisation of territorial transformations; Conclusiones

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a conceptual and observational analysis of Colombia's 2016 differential schemes for rural and hard-to-reach water supply, read in full text 2026-10-04. The urban-rural dichotomy underlying the regulation misfits territories; new categories proposed. No systematic data collection reported.
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate. Methods are unspecified (observations and testimonies), so this is a weak-evidence conceptual paper (cf. A12).
